summary.intent: Run a full GSD milestone-management session for CipherBox: dashboard the milestone, finish/verify Phase 69, discuss Phase 71, plan/execute/ship Phase 70, resolve its PR reviews, insert a new Phase 70.1 to cover a discovered soundness gap, and discuss that new phase's design decisions.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 confirmed already-shipped and marked complete; Phase 71 discussed with 9 decisions locked in 71-CONTEXT.md; Phase 70 planned, executed (8 plans), had a real concurrent-add rotation bug caught by the live sdk-e2e gate and fixed, then shipped as merged PR #596 with all review threads resolved (incl. a CRITICAL anti-rollback TOCTOU fix); a depth-gap residual from PR review became Phase 70.1, inserted and merged as PR #597; Phase 70.1 was then discussed, locking 4 major decisions (ECIES-based key persistence for crash-resume, combined atomic durable record, threaded reconcile generation, adversarial depth-3 e2e fixture) into 70.1-CONTEXT.md, committed on its own branch.

repo: GSD manager's init.manager phase-completeness check globs `*PLAN*.md` and can miscount a research file (e.g. `69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md`) as an extra plan, falsely showing a fully-complete phase as `partial`; the strict `verify phase-completeness N` command is the reliable check.
`.claude/settings.local.json` is gitignored and safe to edit directly (unlike committed `settings.json`); it can hold a `worktree.bgIsolation: "none"` override to unblock Write-tool guards.

Backgrounding GSD manager plan/execute on Claude Code shares the single checkout with the foreground session, causing branch collisions (a background planner can switch the shared working tree onto its own feature branch mid-session) — manager plan/execute should run inline on Claude Code, only Codex safely backgrounds them.
CodeRabbit's PR summary review skips draft PRs, but `greptile-apps` still posts inline review threads on drafts; running the CodeRabbit CLI locally before opening a draft PR covers that gap.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility — PR body edits must go through `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.

The git commit helper can report a timeout/failure (often from 1Password SSH signing or lint-staged) while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying blindly.
`git rebase -i` is unavailable in this environment; conventional-commit subject rewording is done via `git filter-branch --msg-filter`.

The rotation crash-resume job record (`RotationJobRecord`) persists only `completedNodeIds` + a key-source frontier, never the newly-minted post-rotation read key — deliberate 'no keys at rest' design that creates an unrecoverable-key window on crash (Pitfall 4).
`nodeKeySource` in the rotation engine supplies write keys only, never read keys — read keys are minted fresh per rotation and not derivable from any parent/checkpoint.
`vaults.owner_id` (FK, unique-indexed) is the authoritative user→root binding; `ipns_records.user_id` is explicitly documented as a denormalized creator marker only, not an authority source.

Post-Phase-67 TEE lease-renewer structurally cannot repoint a CID on republish (its request body has no `metadataCid` field) — same-sequence + different-CID is always an anomaly, never a legitimate republish.

code.finding: rotateOne mints the new read key in memory only (crypto.getRandomValues), publishes the child via CAS as the crash-safety commit point, then persists completedNodeIds — the new key is never durably checkpointed before publish, creating the depth-gap lost-key window.

Dirty-frontier resume consumption hardcodes parentIpnsName as rootNodeIpnsName instead of using frontierItem.parentIpnsName, making resume depth-1-only — the core bug behind the deferred depth≥2 soundness gap.

createConcurrentAddResealingMerge re-seals a concurrent-add child's SealedChildRef under old-then-new parent key, but this precedent doesn't apply to already-rotated dirty nodes since their key (not the parent's) is what changed and is lost.

createInvite copies dto.rootIpnsName and dto.rootNodeId verbatim from untrusted client input with no server-side ownership lookup — any authenticated caller can mint an invite for any well-formed ipnsName.

bump_lock originally didn't cover the full read-check-bump sequence, creating a TOCTOU that allowed a concurrent-resolve rollback around the anti-rollback floor; fixed by widening the lock scope (commit 98a6265b7).

workflow: When a live/integration e2e gate passes, still check whether its test fixture is adversarial enough — Phase 70's gate passed 'vacuously' because Test 4 used a deliberately childless rotation root, masking a real depth≥2 crash-resume bug that only surfaced via later PR review.

Live end-to-end gates that exercise the real client→API round trip can catch bugs unit tests and typecheck miss entirely (the concurrent-add rotation bug requiring a write key the rotator didn't hold).

When background agents do their own git hygiene (branch creation/reset) in a shared checkout, always verify post-completion which commits swept in which files before assuming clean separation — 70's plan agent unintentionally bundled Phase 69's bookkeeping edits into the Phase 70 plans commit.

For decimal phase insertion (e.g. 70.1 following 68.1/68.2 precedent), STATE.md's derived counters (total_phases, completed/percent) are not auto-updated by `phase insert` — reconcile total_phases immediately but leave derived completion percentages for the next full GSD state write rather than half-fixing them.

friction: Write-tool background-isolation guard blocked committing CONTEXT.md/DISCUSSION-LOG.md to the shared checkout during Phase 71 discussion, requiring a settings.local.json edit to disable it.

The backgrounded Phase 70 planning agent switched the shared working tree to its own feature branch mid-session, stranding uncommitted Phase 69-completion edits and Phase 71 discussion artifacts on the wrong branch — required careful post-hoc separation into distinct branches/PRs.
execute-phase's branch-name computation truncated differently than the plan agent's branch name, requiring a manual `git branch -m` to reconcile before execution could proceed.
Four non-conventional `feat 70-02:` commit subjects from the executor agent required a `git filter-branch` reword pass before the PR could pass the conventional-commit CI gate.
zsh array syntax (`declare -A`, `${!arr[@]}`) failed in the Bash tool during PR-thread resolution, requiring a rewrite as a Node .cjs script.
GitHub GraphQL API calls for PR review threads repeatedly timed out/flaked, requiring retry-wrapped mutations.
The sdk-e2e live-stack recipe wasn't documented in the obvious README location — had to trace through docs/DEVELOPMENT.md to find the correct docker-compose + API bring-up sequence.
Commit operations twice appeared to time out (2 min, exit 143) due to 1Password SSH signing, requiring manual verification via git log rather than blind retries.
A 10th PR review thread appeared after pushing fix commits (reviewers re-reviewing new commits), requiring an extra triage/resolve pass.
open_items: Phase 70.1 ('Rotation Read-Plane Durability and Deep Crash-Resume Soundness') is discussed (CONTEXT.md + DISCUSSION-LOG.md committed on its own branch) but not yet planned or executed.
Phase 71 (Share-Invite Security and IPNS Data-Integrity) is discussed with 9 decisions locked but not yet planned — sits on branch feat/phase-71-share-invite-security.
The rotation-hardening-followups todo retains 2 open items (cross-store floor atomicity, reconcile cached generation) now folded into Phase 70.1's scope but not yet implemented.
Phase 71's rootNodeId validation gap remains an accepted residual — server can verify ownership of rootIpnsName but rootNodeId stays client-asserted unless a new column is added.
STATE.md's derived completed_phases/percent counters were left stale after the Phase 70.1 insertion, pending reconciliation on the next full GSD state write.
Phase 70.1's ECIES wrapped-key checkpoint design requires new GC/lifecycle logic (delete on parent-mirror commit, expire abandoned jobs) that was locked as a decision but not yet implemented.
